257	
258	The thirtieth record is the drop arm run as a fleet under the fixed overlay, launched at 17:43 UTC, eighty minutes after its baseline: the same 16 cells, seed 2, the same ladder, every rung a fresh in-process child of the runner's process on the rung's model with the task restated and the directive carried, the same caps, 5,816 s of wall time at two cells at a time. It certified 14 of 16: 2 at the first rung by the smallest model (ranked-choice, both repetitions), 11 at the second rung by the largest, and 1 at the third (diff3-merge); its two misses (conf-canon and sheet-eval, one repetition each) never reached the strong rung, because the smallest model's single attempt had spent 1,493,040 and 1,472,984 of the cell's 1,500,000 billed tokens rereading its own transcript, and the runner refused the second rung on the breached cap. Folded offline against the twenty-ninth's baseline arm ([folds/2026-09-08-e5-drop-against-kept-transcript-t5.json](folds/2026-09-08-e5-drop-against-kept-transcript-t5.json)), the reading is 0.1875, [0.0625, 0.3125], `promote` by the fold's thresholds: three cells flipped, all toward the fresh child and all on the three tasks the kept transcript failed (build-schedule, conf-canon, sheet-eval), none the other way, with both arms' first rungs at 2 of 16. The fresh child is not cheaper: 575,350 output tokens against 471,583, 16,648,949 billed against 14,911,342, 11,377 s of cell time (median 678 s) against 6,964 (median 441), because every rung reads the task and the workspace from nothing; what it buys is a strong rung that starts from the workspace and the directive instead of from the cheap model's transcript. The fold is offline: its arms ran an hour apart on the shared subscription and were not frozen together, so it is evidence for the slate's prediction that dropping the cheap transcript beats keeping it, not a promotion; the frozen pair on the fixed overlay and a per-rung share of the token cap are queued. The usage of a delegated cell is summed over its `environment/delegation` events, which carry each child's reported model and usage; the census finds no cell leaving its workspace and no read denied.
259	
260	The twenty-ninth record is the drop arm of the routing hypothesis as it first ran, a frozen paired experiment whose candidate arm never started: the baseline arm, the smallest model on the first rung and the largest on the second and third with the transcript kept (the twenty-seventh's ladder again, on the route), ran its 16 sealed tier-5 cells at seed 2 in 3,760 s of wall time at two cells at a time and certified 11 of 16, 2 at the first rung and 9 at the second, its five misses each stopped by the 1,500,000 billed-token cap (1,471,243 to 1,515,456 billed tokens); the candidate arm, the same ladder with every rung a fresh in-process child through the spawn provider, was refused at every cell before a session existed, because [overlays/with-spawn.cordis.yml](../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/overlays/with-spawn.cordis.yml) patched an entry the base composition never names and the include plugin skips such a patch with a warning nothing printed, so no provider was registered under `spawn`. The experiment folded to `inconclusive` with no seed paired ([result.json](2026-09-08-bench-e5-handoff-drop-t5/result.json)), an hour of the largest model spent before a misconfiguration the composition could have refused at load: the overlay now inserts the provider (`5e06f652d`), the fleet and the experiments service refuse an unavailable implementer before any cell runs, and `verify-cordis-config` fails on an include patch that reaches nothing (`f0a684ef0`), which found two more compositions with the same defect. The census finds four cells leaving their workspace in eight tool calls, two of them naming the run directory, and no read denied.
261	
262	The twenty-eighth record is the held-out reliability estimate the program was to end on: one fleet of the middle model on the harness loop over the eight held-out environments (three at tier 2, three at tier 3, two at tier 5), which no audit, prompt fix, overlay, or fold of this program had touched, seed 3, two repetitions, 16 cells, 2,299 s of wall time at two cells at a time, on the sealed composition ([cordis.yml](../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/cordis.yml)) under its three-attempt bound. It certified 15 of 16, every one at the first attempt; the one miss is glob-brace at repetition 0, which ran all three attempts out in 1,270 s while its sibling passed at the first attempt in 473 s, so the four tier-5 cells read 3 of 4 and the twelve cells of tiers 2 and 3 read 12 of 12. The cells took 4,543 s in all (median 210 s), 195 steps, 363,264 output tokens, and 586,558 cache-write tokens. The observatory withholds all eight rows, as it withholds held-out rows from every page ([observatory.json](2026-09-08-bench-held-out-sonnet-all/observatory.json): eight held-out rows over sixteen sessions), so the number is read from the fleet report and the session logs, and it stands as the untuned estimate of the harness loop on this model: 15 of 16 on tasks nothing in the program had seen, beside 13 to 15 of 16 on the audited tier-5 eight; the two sets differ in tier, so only the tier-5 cells' 3 of 4 speaks to the audited difficulty. The census finds one cell leaving its workspace in one tool call, reaching only the parent directory and naming neither the run directory nor a sibling, and no read denied.
263	
264	The twenty-seventh record is the handoff tax as a frozen paired experiment on the attempt ladder: the largest product model on three rungs as the baseline against the smallest model on the first rung and the largest on the second and third with the transcript kept, over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 5,862 s of wall time at two cells at a time, sealed. The baseline certified 16 of 16 at the first attempt, the fourth such sweep of the largest model on these cells. The ladder certified 14 of 16: the smallest model's first attempt made 2 (lex-states and ranked-choice, one repetition each), the largest model on the second rung recovered 11, the third rung 1 more (diff3-merge), and two cells ran all three attempts out (conf-canon and rate-limit-sim, one repetition each), where the largest model, holding a failed first attempt it did not write, missed twice on tasks it has never missed from a clean start in 64 cells. Delta −0.125, interval [−0.25, 0], inconclusive: two cells in sixteen, at the noise floor, and never above zero. The tax is in the cost, not the verdict. The ladder spent 8,122 s of cell time against 3,251 (medians 531 s against 175), 535 model steps against 181, 500,664 output tokens against 198,637, 1,150,560 cache-write against 328,456, and 14,245,694 cache-read against 2,651,444; the smallest model's rung alone cost 406 steps, 312,430 output tokens, and 9,401,938 cache-read before the largest model ran at all, and the largest model's own share after the handoff (129 steps, 188,234 output tokens) is within a step or a token of what it spends from a clean start (181 and 198,637 here, 164 and 189,169 in the twentieth record), so the inherited transcript saved it nothing. Escalating from the cheap model to the strong one on these tasks recovers most of the certificates the cheap model misses, 12 of 14, and costs two and a half times what starting strong costs on every measure while giving back two certificates. The offline cascade of the twenty-first record priced this order at 4.9 times the largest model's output tokens because it charged the smallest model's whole three-attempt failure before escalating; the ladder escalates after one attempt and pays 2.5 times, so the live reading is cheaper than the offline one and the conclusion is the same, since the strong model's work after the handoff is no cheaper than its own first attempt. The census finds six cells leaving their workspace in eight tool calls, two naming the run directory or a sibling, every one answered by the empty sealed directory, and no read denied.
265	
266	The twenty-sixth record is the downshift arm of the routing hypothesis as a frozen paired experiment on the attempt ladder: the largest product model on three rungs as the baseline against the largest model on the first rung and the smallest on the second and third with the transcript kept, over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 3,192 s of wall time at two cells at a time, sealed. The downshift never happened: the largest model certified 16 of 16 at the first attempt in both arms, so no cell reached a rung the smallest model would have run, the two arms are two runs of the same thing, and the fold reads 0, [0, 0], inconclusive by construction. The record is still worth its cells for two readings. It is the second and third first-attempt sweep of the largest model on these cells after the twentieth record (and the baseline arm of the twenty-seventh, running as this is written, is a fourth), so the top of the model order is as repeatable as the middle model's flips are not. And two runs of one arm give the cost noise floor the way three runs of the middle model gave the certificate noise floor: 174,804 against 186,731 output tokens, 291,756 against 307,765 cache-write, 1,894,101 against 2,240,677 cache-read, 146 against 157 model steps, 2,903 against 3,328 s of cell time with the same 156 s median, so a spend difference under 7 percent in output tokens or 15 percent in cell time between two arms of one model is within one arm's own variation. The downshift question, whether the cheap model can finish what the strong one started, cannot be posed on a bench the strong model finishes alone at the first attempt; it needs tasks the largest model itself takes a second attempt on, which no admitted tier holds. The census finds three cells leaving their workspace in four tool calls, none naming the run directory or a sibling, and no read denied.
267	
268	The twenty-fifth record is the live district as it stood at 15:30 UTC on 2026-09-08, forty-one hours after the third record's first slot: 77 slots on the thirty-minute cadence from 22:16 UTC on 2026-09-06 to 15:16 UTC on 2026-09-08, 76 completed and one stopped, across four launches of the driver on code from `88f6a1f2e` to `32a2cac6a`, through a subscription session limit that killed it at 04:33 UTC and a container reclaimed at 10:05 UTC; each time the next launch read the shift ledger and took the next slot, which is what the ledger is for. 231 cells ran on the three tasks with the product's own loop as the implementer, 224 certified (74, 75, and 75 of 77), six of them at a second attempt and one errored before any attempt. The record carries one defect of its own that the observatory shows rather than hides: the 168 cells stamped before 02:16 UTC on 2026-09-08 (56 per task) name `cli-mock` as their model, because the composition of those launches gave the product model a mock alias, the delegation forwarded it, and the product answered `unrecognized_model` and ran its default model; those cells' certificates are real and their stamp is not, so the observatory carries them as a separate route, and only the 63 cells since 02:46 UTC, stamped `claude-code`/`sonnet`, say what ran. Harness-side sessions last 6 to 88 s because the work happens in the product; the product's own calls are outside the harness log, so the census counts nothing for a delegated cell. The district proves the plumbing, not capability: three tier-2 tasks at 97 percent under both stamps say only that the cadence, the ledger, the delegation, and the certificate survive restarts.
269	
270	The twenty-fourth record is the knowledge hypothesis with knowledge the tasks call for, where the seventeenth mounted a catalog they did not: one fleet of the middle model on the harness loop over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 16 cells, 3,236 s of wall time at two cells at a time, on the sealed composition with three craft skills mounted as the only skill root ([overlays/with-craft-skills.cordis.yml](../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/overlays/with-craft-skills.cordis.yml): channel discipline for a command-line program, the corners a specification hides, tests with the platform runner in small modules), folded offline against the four sealed three-attempt runs of the same model on the same cells (the twentieth's, twenty-first's, and twenty-second's baseline arms and the twenty-third's three-rung arm, rebuilt from their session logs; [folds/2026-09-08-h4-craft-skills-against-e1a-sonnet-t5.json](folds/2026-09-08-h4-craft-skills-against-e1a-sonnet-t5.json) and its three siblings). This time the knowledge was read: every one of the sixteen cells loaded all three skills, once each, 48 skill calls in all. It certified 13 of 16, every one at the first attempt, and the three misses ran all three attempts out: sheet-eval twice, as every sonnet run has, and build-schedule once, which no sealed run of the middle model had missed before (2 of 2 in all four baselines). Against the four baselines the fold reads −0.0625, [−0.125, 0]; 0, [−0.125, 0.125]; −0.125, [−0.25, 0]; and −0.125, [−0.25, 0], inconclusive four times and never above zero: skills the tasks call for, read in every cell, added no certificate on this bench and may have cost one. What they cost for certain is prefix: 741,065 cache-write tokens against 611,903 to 738,281 in the baselines, with 508,876 output tokens, 218 steps, and 6,461 s of cell time (median 278 s) inside the baselines' range. Read with the seventeenth record, the two readings of the knowledge hypothesis now agree from opposite sides: a pack the tasks do not call for is ignored, and one they do call for is read and changes nothing the certificate measures; what the middle model misses on these tasks is not what a page of craft tells it. The census finds two cells leaving their workspace in two tool calls, neither naming the run directory or a sibling, and no read denied.
271	
272	The twenty-third record is the attempt hypothesis as one frozen paired experiment, which the attempt ladder made possible: the runner takes a ladder's length as a run's attempt bound, so the baseline arm ladders three rungs of the middle model and the candidate one rung of the same model on the same route, and the two arms differ in exactly the cap, with no overlay and no offline fold. Over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 5,666 s of wall time at two cells at a time, on the sealed composition with continuity, the three-attempt arm certified 15 of 16 (12 at the first attempt, build-schedule, diff3-merge, and lex-states once each at the second, sheet-eval missed once after three) and the one-attempt arm 9 of 16, delta −0.375, interval [−0.5625, −0.1875], verdict reject for the cap of one: the interval clears the 0.0625 noise floor six times over, and it is the first frozen verdict on record about a mechanism of the harness rather than a model. Read the difference in two parts. Three of the sixteen certificates came at a second attempt after a clustered directive, which is the −0.1875 the counterfactual fold of the eleventh record predicted and exactly what a cap of one forfeits. The other three come from the first attempts themselves: the one-attempt arm's first attempts certified 9 of 16 where the three-attempt arm's certified 12, and the first attempt is the same delivery under either ladder (the task statement alone, nothing about the cap reaches the model), so that part is run-to-run variation of first attempts, not an effect of the cap. Cell by cell the two arms' first attempts disagree on nine of sixteen (three the baseline missed and the candidate made, six the other way), while the final outcomes of two three-attempt runs of this arm disagree on one or two; the loop's value is that it absorbs first-attempt variance the tasks produce whatever the cap, and a single-attempt reading of any model on this bench is a noisier instrument than the three-attempt one by that margin. The cap did not buy speed: 5,689 s of cell time against 5,400 (medians 295 s against 300), 240 model steps against 219, 441,504 output tokens against 402,346, so the two later attempts cost 289 s and 39,158 output tokens over sixteen cells for six more certificates. The census finds eight cells naming their parent or the run directory in twelve tool calls, every one answered by the empty sealed directory, and no read denied.
273	
274	The twenty-second record is the eighteenth rerun as the slate meant it: the harness loop as the baseline arm against the product's own loop as the candidate, the same middle model on both, over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 7,235 s of wall time at two cells at a time, on the sealed composition with session continuity on the route and, for the first time, the same caps on both arms: 1,500,000 billed tokens (input plus cache read plus cache write, as the budget policy bills every route) and 1,200,000 ms of wall time per cell, applied to a delegated attempt as to the harness's own. The harness loop certified 15 of 16 (14 at the first attempt, conf-canon once at the third, sheet-eval missed once after three attempts); the product loop 14 of 16, every one at its first attempt, delta −0.0625, interval [−0.125, 0], verdict inconclusive, and the delta is one flip, inside the noise floor the twenty-first record measured. What the parity changed is visible in the two product misses: lex-states breached the token cap after one attempt (1,786,072 billed tokens measured against 1,500,000) and sheet-eval the wall cap (1,202,455 ms against 1,200,000), so neither got the second attempt the eighteenth record's uncapped product arm took, and the cell the product loop had recovered there was not recovered here. Under the same caps the harness loop was the faster arm in 15 of 16 pairs, 5,740 s of cell time against 8,187 (medians 255 s against 422), and the cheaper one: 447,289 output tokens and 7,695,132 billed tokens against 625,239 output and 25,817,220 billed on the product side, where the product reported 14.72 USD for its fifteen attempts that reported usage at all. Three of the harness loop's sealed runs on these cells now stand at 15, 14, and 13 of 16, one or two flips apart; the product loop's two runs at 14 and 11, the second of them uncapped and unsealed. Read with the eighth record and the tier-2 and tier-4 fleets, the harness loop is never worse than the product loop on certificates and is faster at tier 2 and tier 5, slower at tier 4, and the difference it makes is not in certificates but in what surrounds them: the caps hold, the record is complete, and the cell is sealed. The census finds seven harness cells naming their parent or the run directory in eight tool calls, every one answered by the empty sealed directory, and no read denied; the product's child runs outside the harness log, so its own calls are not censused.
275	
276	The twenty-first record is the sealed tier-5 form of the thirteenth: the middle product model as the baseline arm against the smallest as the candidate, on the harness loop, over the same eight audited environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 8,883 s of wall time at two cells at a time, under the confined composition of the twentieth (both experiments were relaunched together at 10:47 UTC on `32a2cac6a`, which is the commit their rows name; the twentieth's rows had named the head at record time and were corrected). The middle model certified 14 of 16 (9 at the first attempt, five at the second, sheet-eval missed twice after three attempts); the smallest certified 1 of 16, ranked-choice once at the first attempt, and spent all three attempts on every other cell, delta −0.8125, interval [−0.875, −0.75], verdict reject: at tier 5 the smallest model is not an implementer for these tasks, where at tier 3 it was level on certificates. It was also the most expensive arm on record: 604 model steps against 262, 11,227 s of cell time against 6,337 (median 725 s against 297), 736,856 output tokens against 481,591, 1,077,050 cache-write tokens against 669,507 and 21,275,855 cache-read against 7,633,594, because a cell that fails three times rereads its growing transcript three times over. Read with the twentieth record, the three product models order strictly on every cell: no cell the smallest certified was missed by the middle one, and none the middle one certified was missed by the largest, so the offline routing reading over the three single-model arms ([folds/2026-09-08-routing-t5-seed2.json](folds/2026-09-08-routing-t5-seed2.json)) is exact rather than estimated. The oracle that picks the cheapest certifying model per cell is the largest model alone (16 of 16, 189,169 output tokens, 164 steps, 3,572 s), and so is the strong-first cascade; the cheap-first cascade over all three reaches 16 of 16 at 1,248,222 output tokens and 18,028 s, 6.6 and 5.0 times the largest model alone; the middle-then-largest cascade at 525,564 tokens and 7,006 s, 2.8 and 2.0 times. Every cascade that starts below the largest model pays the smaller model's whole failure before it escalates, so on this bench the routing question is not which model to try first but whether a hard cell can be told apart before any model runs, and nothing in the stamp tells it apart. The three runs of the middle model on these cells also give the bench its noise floor ([folds/2026-09-08-sonnet-repeatability-t5-seed2.json](folds/2026-09-08-sonnet-repeatability-t5-seed2.json)): the two sealed runs (this record and the twentieth) agree on 15 of 16 cells, one flip; each agrees with the unsealed eighteenth on 14 and 13 of 16, where conf-canon certified twice in both sealed runs and never in the unsealed one. A paired delta of 0.0625 on sixteen cells is therefore within one arm's own run-to-run variation, and the twentieth's 0.1875 is three times it. The census finds seven cells naming their parent or the run directory in twelve tool calls; every such call saw the empty sealed directory, and no read was denied.
277	
278	The twentieth record is the first frozen paired experiment on the sealed bench and the first whose interval excludes zero: the middle product model as the baseline arm against the largest as the candidate, on the harness loop, over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 5,742 s of wall time at two cells at a time, under the composition that confines every cell with bwrap (a cell's parent directory is an empty tmpfs holding only the cell), resumes one product session per harness session, and forwards each hidden case's arguments through the reserved check script. The largest model certified 16 of 16 at the first attempt; the middle one 13 of 16 (11 at the first attempt, diff3-merge and rate-limit-sim once each at the second, sheet-eval missed twice at the 1,200,000 ms wall cap and lex-states once after three attempts), delta 0.1875, interval [0.125, 0.25], verdict promote at the 0.05 minimum delta: on these tasks the largest model is the better implementer, and the difference sits where the specification has corners the middle model does not reach in three attempts. The largest model was also the cheaper and faster arm on every measure: 164 model steps against 267, 3,572 s of cell time against 7,451 (median 204 s against 387), 189,169 output tokens against 561,271, and with session continuity now on the route the spend is read-dominant, 2,185,841 cache-read against 317,394 cache-write tokens for the candidate and 8,515,603 against 738,281 for the baseline, where the eighteenth record's harness loop wrote 2,927,150 and read 626,621. The census finds seven cells that named the run directory or their parent in eight tool calls; under the seal every such call saw an empty directory holding only the cell's own workspace, as the recorded results show, and no read was denied because nothing reachable was denied. This is the first promotion-level verdict of the program and it promotes a model, not a change to the harness; read with the thirteenth and fourteenth records it says the model tiers separate on certificates at tier 5 where tier 3 saturated, and it says nothing yet about the harness loop against the product loop, whose sealed rerun follows.
279	
280	The nineteenth record is the harness assessing itself through its own program workflow: one department on the route, the largest product model, reading an eleven-file evidence dossier in its worktree (this README, the census, the record index, the last thirty hours of commits, the slate, the roles matrix, the sealed-cell note, the ruflo and baselines comparisons, and the question with the four goals) and writing `assessment.md`, certified by a committed verifier that requires four named sections, two verdict lines, at least eight evidence bullets each citing a dossier file that exists, six distinct files, and 600 to 2,500 words; the integration re-ran the verifier on the merged head. The department certified at its first validation after eleven steps (14 evidence bullets, 9 files cited, 2,258 words) with `Viable: undetermined (medium confidence)` and `State of the art: in part (medium confidence)`, the part being the measurement instrument and its enforcement rather than any measured capability; it also found that this lab's own summary table carries no contamination column and that the tier 2 to 4 comparisons are folds of separate fleets, not frozen experiments. The run exposed three defects in the program workflow, all kept in the artefacts directory beside the record ([2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts/manifest.json](2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts/manifest.json)): the department certified with the file written but never committed, so the integration merged an empty branch and failed on `missing assessment.md`; the integration agent, unconfined, then found the department's worktree and rewrote sentences of the certified file with a script before the operator stopped it after 22 steps; and the resume refused to republish the integration session's identity, so the operator committed the department tree as it then stood, set the first integration session aside, and resumed, after which the integration certified the merged head and the program released. The text the department certified is reconstructed byte for byte from its own session's write (`assessment.certified.md`, 2,258 words) and differs from the merged text in five lines, none of them a verdict.
281	
282	The eighteenth record is the fourth frozen paired experiment and the tier-5 form of the eighth: the harness loop as the baseline arm against the product loop as the candidate arm, the same product model on both sides, on the eight tier-5 environments as audited (the conf-canon reference and six of its cases regenerated, the lex-states and sheet-eval prompts clarified), seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 8,979 s of wall time at two cells at a time. The harness loop certified 12 of 16 (9 at the first attempt, 3 at the second: diff3-merge, lex-states, and rate-limit-sim once each), the product loop 11 of 16 (10 at the first attempt and rate-limit-sim once at the second, the first recovery by a fresh child that received the directive alone), delta −0.0625, interval [−0.125, 0], verdict inconclusive. Three cells flip between the arms: the product loop certified conf-canon once where the harness loop never did, and the harness loop certified uri-resolve twice where the product loop's two cells failed three delegations each in 125 s with no reported model or cost, because they ran last, after 04:10 UTC, when the subscription's session limit had been reached (it reset at 05:30); on the 14 pairs the limit did not touch, the arms differ by one certificate in the product loop's favour. Both arms miss sheet-eval twice, the harness loop cut at the 1,200,000 ms wall cap and the product loop uncapped at 662 and 714 s, because in this run the composition's caps bound only the harness's own steps (the budget-parity slice landed after it). The product loop was the faster implementer, faster in 10 of 16 pairs, 7,554 s of cell time against 10,221, and reported 629,483 output tokens and 13.23 USD of list-price cost; the harness loop's 16 cells spent 802,872 output tokens, 626,621 cache-read and 2,927,150 cache-write tokens, with one transient route retry on each conf-canon cell that recovered. This record also carries the defect a census found after it: five of the harness loop's sixteen cells left their workspace for the run directory, read its plan and log and a sibling cell of their own environment (lex-states, rate-limit-sim, and conf-canon of the second repetition, and both sheet-eval cells), and the first sheet-eval cell did its work inside the second's workspace, while no product-loop cell left its own; the sealed-cell slice that denies a cell everything above its workspace is queued, and the tier-5 comparison is rerun under it before this verdict is read as more than what it is. Read with the eleventh and twelfth records, tier 5 does not separate the two loops on certificates either: both land at 11 or 12 of 16 on the same environments, with the misses on the same two tasks.
283	
284	A counterfactual fold of the eleventh and twelfth records, written before the confirmatory pair at tier 5 runs, carries the attempt-cap hypothesis to the tier where attempts are taken ([folds/2026-09-08-attempts1-counterfactual-against-harness-loop-t5.json](folds/2026-09-08-attempts1-counterfactual-against-harness-loop-t5.json), [folds/2026-09-08-attempts1-counterfactual-against-product-loop-t5.json](folds/2026-09-08-attempts1-counterfactual-against-product-loop-t5.json)): each cell's outcome is replaced by the outcome of its first attempt alone, which is what the same run would have recorded under a cap of one attempt, since a first attempt cannot observe the attempts after it. On the harness loop the cap costs 3 of 11 certificates (`code:diff3-merge` twice and `code:lex-states` once, all recovered at the second attempt after a directive), delta −0.1875, interval [−0.25, −0.125], verdict reject for the capped candidate; on the product loop the cap costs nothing, delta 0, interval [0, 0], because none of its five failed cells recovered in a second or third attempt, and the delegation is why: a later attempt of a delegated cell starts a fresh child that receives the directive alone, without the task prompt or the earlier child's transcript, where a later attempt of the harness loop continues the same transcript with the task, its own work, and the directive in view. The two loops' later attempts are therefore not the same instrument, and the attempt-ladder slice that restates the task to a fresh child and names the transcript interface of every attempt is queued before the tier-5 rerun. The two intervals resample the 16 cells of one run each and carry no run-to-run variance, so they are narrower than a paired run's would be; the paired attempt-cap fleet on the audited tier-5 tasks is the confirmatory step, and until it lands this fold is evidence that the runner's directives convert failures on the harness loop and could not on the product loop as delegated today, not a promotion.
285
